entities.summary: Caspar Röist was a Swiss papal official and commander of the papacy's Swiss Guard, appointed in 1517 by Pope Leo X. He played a key role in the defense of Rome against the forces of Charles V, Emperor of the Holy Roman Empire, during the Sack of Rome in 1527. This event was a devastating blow to the Catholic Church and marked the beginning of a period of decline in papal power and influence. Röist's leadership during this event has been the subject of debate among historians, with some praising his bravery and others criticizing his role in the sack. The Sack of Rome had significant consequences for the Catholic Church, leading to a period of reform and the eventual establishment of the Jesuit Order. Röist's legacy is complex and multifaceted, reflecting both the bravery and the brutality of the events he was a part of.
